theory.title: Exercise 2.3.4: Templates with Variables
theory.content:
MENTOR-9: "Hardcoded test data is brittle. Change one threshold, and you edit 50 data rows. Use variables instead—change once, update everywhere. That's maintainable automation."

Variables in Template Data

Template data rows can use variables for flexibility:

*** Variables ***
${API_URL}     https://api.example.com
${TIMEOUT}     30
@{ENDPOINTS}   /users    /posts    /comments

*** Keywords ***
Check Endpoint
    [Arguments]    ${endpoint}    ${expected_code}
    Log    GET ${API_URL}${endpoint}
    # Validation logic here

*** Test Cases ***
API Validation
    [Template]    Check Endpoint
    ${ENDPOINTS}[0]    200
    ${ENDPOINTS}[1]    200
    ${ENDPOINTS}[2]    200

Benefits:

  • Change ${API_URL} once, updates all tests
  • List variables for repeated test subjects
  • Scalar variables for thresholds, limits, constants
  • Easier to maintain large test suites

Example: Threshold Testing

*** Variables ***
${MIN_TEMP}    -20
${MAX_TEMP}    80

*** Keywords ***
Validate Temperature
    [Arguments]    ${location}    ${temp}
    Log    ${location}: ${temp}°C
    Should Be True    ${temp} >= ${MIN_TEMP}
    Should Be True    ${temp} <= ${MAX_TEMP}
    Log    Temperature within safe range

*** Test Cases ***
Temperature Validation
    [Template]    Validate Temperature
    Engine Room      ${45}
    Bridge          ${22}
    Cargo Bay       ${-5}
    Reactor         ${75}

Change ${MIN_TEMP} or ${MAX_TEMP}, all validations update automatically.

⚠️ Variable + Template Best Practices

  • Use *** Variables *** section for constants and lists
  • Reference variables in template data rows
  • List variables: access with ${list}[index]
  • Makes test data maintainable and configurable
  • Great for: API URLs, thresholds, test subjects, configuration
  • Combine with FOR loops for even more power (advanced)
